families.title: Permissions tied to building history or conditions
families.clause: 621 (B): a building existing on 28 Feb 1977 may be replaced if the new height does not exceed the old. 937 (I): an office is permitted in a detached house that existed in 1988 if (i) software production only, (ii) 1989 parking and landscaping retained. 350 (E): a multiple family dwelling is permitted on 195 Danforth Rd. if (i) one unit per 99 m2 of lot, (ii) 4.5 m from the front lot line.

keyings.B: PERMIT / REQUIRE (621 (B) PERMIT; 937 (I)(i) PERMIT, (ii) REQUIRE); LIMIT front_setback_m 4.5 (350 (E)(ii))

families.question: Is a permission whose use or building depends on a date or on listed conditions kept UNUSUAL on the rule-31 route, with the conditions UNUSUAL too?
families.why: Keying rule 31 (building-history clauses never a bare PERMIT/REQUIRE) and keying rule 27 (the conditions of a "permitted if:" clause are UNUSUAL, never REQUIRE) already say so; keyer B read the leaves as stand-alone rules. A plain LIMIT front_setback_m on 350 (E)(ii) would impose 4.5 m on every lot, but it is a condition of one named permission.
families.recText: UNUSUAL, existing-building route; disclose the dated condition.
families.cite: Spec 133 §m.317 (keying rule 31); §m.105 dated note, rule 27; agreed twins 1436 (B)(iv), 1437 (B)(iv) and 958/951 (D)(E).

families.title: Setback arm for named roads ("where the lot line abuts Finch Ave., ...")
families.clause: The minimum building setback from a lot line that abuts a street is (i) 7.5 metres where the lot line abuts <named roads>.
families.question: Is a setback arm that applies only on named roads UNUSUAL?
families.why: No lot data names the road a lot line abuts. A plain LIMIT would apply 7.5 m to every lot, over-restricting (Spec 133 M-130: the expressible bound must be necessary on every lot). The 267 (D)(i) and 324 (D)(i) arms are already UNUSUAL this way.
families.cite: Spec 133 §m.136 (setback from a lot line abutting a named road is UNUSUAL, keying rule 24); §m.130.

families.title: "In all other cases" / "any other street" setback arms
families.clause: (ii) 6.0 metres where the lot line abuts any other street / 4.5 metres in all other cases where the side lot line abuts a street.
families.question: May a complement arm ("all other streets") be a LIMIT, and which target for a side lot line?
families.why: EVE.R6-2 made 324 (D)(ii) a LIMIT. A complement arm is a true necessary bound only when it is the smallest of its sibling arms (M-130); in 1029 the arms are 7.5, 6.0 and 3.6, so (ii) 6.0 would over-restrict where 3.6 applies. For 200 (C)(ii) the wording is a side lot line, so side_setback_street_m (EVE.M324-G).

options.t: LIMIT when the arm is the smallest sibling, UNUSUAL otherwise; side lot line takes side_setback_street_m

families.recText: LIMIT only where the complement value is the minimum of its arms (278 (C)(ii)/(D)(ii) 6.0; 200 (C)(ii) 4.5 with side_setback_street_m; 1121 (C)(ii) 6.0); UNUSUAL for 1029 (C)(ii) 6.0 and (iii) 3.6 mixed arms.
families.cite: Spec 133 §m.130 (necessary bound); EVE.R6-2 (pattern door); EVE.M324-G (named yard decides). Extending M-130 to complement arms is NEW RULING NEEDED.

draft.register: Spec 69a, new row next to M-130
draft.row: An "all other cases / any other street" arm is keyed as a LIMIT only when its value is the minimum of its sibling arms for the same target; otherwise UNUSUAL. A side lot line arm takes side_setback_street_m.
draft.fiveWords: standardized (one test: smallest sibling); observable (the unit shows the value and its siblings); accurate (never over-restricts); scalable (all complement arms); understandable (one sentence); no scope creep (no new target).

families.lotsNote: 278 (179) alone; 1029 (224) and 1121 (224) also need FAM-ABUT-NAMED; 200 (182) also needs FAM-ARMS.

families.title: Per-subject arms ("per semi-detached house and ... each dwelling unit")
families.clause: (i) minimum lot frontage is 15.0 metres per semi-detached house and 7.5 metres for each dwelling unit; (iii) minimum lot area is 510 m2 per semi-detached house and 250 m2 for each dwelling unit.

keyings.A: required_lot_frontage_m = 7.5 m x dwelling_units (area: 250 x dwelling_units)

families.question: Which expression carries "X per semi-detached house and Y for each dwelling unit"?
families.why: Each keyer kept one arm and dropped the other. Keying rule 30 says per-subject arms, never max() and never a sum; R12-4 keyed the same wording at 331 (A)(ii) as by_type(semi_detached_house: 18.0; other: 9.0 x dwelling_units), which neither keyer wrote here.

options.t: by_type(semi_detached_house: 15.0 m; other: 7.5 m x dwelling_units) (area: 510 m2 / 250 m2 x dwelling_units)

families.cite: Keying rule 30 and brief rule P7 (Spec 133 §m.105 dated note); R12-4 precedent 331 (A)(ii), (B)(ii).

families.title: FSI bound "maximum ... is 0.33" for a named lot
families.clause: The maximum floor space index of the building on the lot known as 19 Barker Ave. is 0.33 / 37 Gibson Ave. is 0.34.
families.question: Bound max or exact?
families.why: The brief maps "maximum" to max and reserves exact for a fixed value with neither word; the clause says "maximum floor space index".
families.cite: Keying brief field rule 4 (bound: "maximum" to max); Spec 68 section 6.
families.lotsNote: Exception 9 has only these two pending units.

families.title: Ancillary-building lot coverage target (971 (D), 975 (D))
families.clause: The maximum lot coverage for ancillary buildings is 5%.
families.question: Which target carries an ancillary-building coverage cap, and does the wording need a licence pattern?
families.why: A lot_coverage_pct of 5 percent would cap the whole lot (M-179(1): ancillary coverage is "never the lot overall coverage"). B has the right target, but its patterns are "ancillary buildings combined", "covered by ancillary buildings and structures"; "lot coverage for ancillary buildings" is not one, so B would fail G-CLAUSE variable_unlicensed.

options.t: ancillary_coverage_pct, with the pattern "lot coverage for ancillary buildings" added

families.cite: Spec 133 §m.132 (pattern growth); M-179(1) via the vocabulary concept. Pattern addition is NEW RULING NEEDED (as EVE.R6-1).

draft.row: Add the licence pattern "lot coverage for ancillary buildings" to ancillary_coverage_pct; 971 (D) and 975 (D) take keyer B.
draft.fiveWords: standardized (the pattern door); observable (gate licenses the unit); accurate (the cap stays on ancillary buildings only); scalable (family of ancillary coverage clauses); understandable; no scope creep (one pattern).

families.title: Stepped side yard "1.8 m ... plus 0.6 m for each additional storey or portion thereof"
families.clause: The minimum side yard setback is 1.8 metres on each side for a one-storey building, plus 0.6 metres for each additional storey or portion thereof.

keyings.B: LIMIT side_setback_m = 1.8 m + 0.6 m x (proposed storeys - 1)

families.question: May a stepped "or portion thereof" schedule be a formula?
families.why: "Or portion thereof" rounds up; the DSL has no ceiling form, so a linear formula under-states the setback for a partial storey (brief rule 20, M-102).
families.cite: Spec 133 §m.102 (a real limit the DSL cannot express is UNUSUAL); brief rule 20 (rounding).

families.title: Front setback for named addresses (929 (F))
families.clause: On the lots municipally known as 145 and 147 Earlton Dr., the minimum front yard building setback is 7.5 metres.
families.question: LIMIT with named_lots_only, or UNUSUAL?
families.why: The same wording is agreed as a LIMIT with status not_modelled / named_lots_only at 393 (F) (58 and 60 Bethune Blvd.), 160 (F) and 128 (C)(i); keyer A alone departed.
families.recText: LIMIT, not modelled for other lots.

families.title: Ancillary structure set back from the residential building (1120 (G)(iii))
families.clause: An ancillary building or structure must be set back a minimum of 3.0 metres from a residential building on the lot.
families.question: Is a set back from a building on the same lot a separation_m LIMIT?
families.why: separation_m is defined as the separation between buildings on the same lot; its patterns include "from the residential building" but not "from a residential building", so B needs one pattern.

options.t: LIMIT separation_m, with the pattern "from a residential building"

families.cite: Spec 133 §m.132; vocabulary concept of separation_m. Pattern is NEW RULING NEEDED (with R10-ALL).

draft.row: Add "from a residential building" to separation_m; 1120 (G)(iii) takes keyer B.
draft.fiveWords: standardized; observable; accurate (same-lot separation); scalable; understandable; no scope creep (one pattern).

families.title: Platform and front-wall entrance prohibitions (1401 (B), (C))
families.clause: (B) a platform higher than the first floor may not encroach into the required front or rear yard; (C) if the lot frontage is 7.6 m or less, a vehicle entrance through the front wall is not permitted.
families.question: Do prohibitions take a setback target?
families.why: Both are prohibitions with no number: "may not encroach" is PROHIBIT with no target (keying rule 28); platform_rear_setback_m is a rear-only reference and (B) also covers the front yard; garage_entrance_setback_m is a setback distance, not a ban.
families.cite: Keying rule 28 (Spec 133 §m.105 dated note); vocabulary concepts of the two targets.

families.title: Parking space length on a named lot (350 (F)(ii))
families.clause: On 46 Scotia Avenue: one required parking space having a minimum length of 4.65 metres may be located in the street yard if it is beside and parallel with the driveway.
families.question: Is 4.65 m a limit or a descriptor of a permitted location?
families.why: The clause permits a location; the length describes the space. A plain LIMIT would impose a 4.65 m minimum length on every lot (M-130).

options.t: PERMIT / UNUSUAL, 4.65 m recorded not modelled

families.cite: Spec 133 §m.130 (necessary bound). Whether a descriptor length is a limit is NEW RULING NEEDED if you want B.

summary.basis: direct census lots of the 13 exceptions whose pending units all sit in these families; an exception unblocks only when every family it needs is settled
